finds.quote: It argues that current doctrine has misclassified machine-mediated composition by generalizing from the autonomous-machine test case to the dialogic craft.
finds.window: U.S. copyright doctrine, Thaler v. Perlmutter (2025; cert. denied 2 March 2026) and registration practice 2023-2025
finds.note: Thesis about how the doctrine came to be (generalization from the autonomous-machine test case); argued in Part I and the 'verdict' (l.90).

finds.quote: Across the intervening century and a half — the typewriter, the synthesizer, the sampler, the camera in all its automations, the digital toolchain — controversies arose and the broad line held: unpredictability or mechanical mediation has not, by itself, defeated authorship where human creative judgment selected, arranged, directed, or fixed the work. Generative AI is the first compositional instrument since 1884 placed on the far side of the *Sarony* line: not a medium authorship flows through but a boundary authorship dies at.
finds.note: Historical thesis: generative AI is the first compositional instrument since 1884 placed outside the instrument classification.

finds.quote: Observe what Thaler actually litigated. Across a decade, in copyright and in the worldwide DABUS patent cases, he *repeatedly disclaimed his own creative input* — structuring the record to force the system to answer not "who owns this" but **"is there a someone here."**
finds.window: Thaler copyright and DABUS patent litigation, across a decade
finds.note: Thesis about what a litigant was doing (structuring the record to force the individuation question).

finds.quote: The predictable equilibrium is concealment — the doctrine manufactures the very opacity about machine contribution that every other policy actor, from the training-disclosure bills to the provenance-standards bodies, is trying to eliminate. A rule that punishes honest attribution is not a provenance regime; it is a confession protocol, and its yield is silence. Stated as a general mechanism for the registry, beyond copyright: **any provenance regime that punishes the provenance it demands will manufacture opacity.**
finds.note: Embedded forecast / general mechanism: disclosure-coupled-to-forfeiture yields concealment; no falsifier or window.

finds.quote: The old catalogs become comparatively privileged investable assets, their scarcity preserved not by creative supremacy but by the de-authoring of a vast share of the living competition.
finds.note: Embedded forecast of catalog-moat effect from the public-domain status of machine-mediated output; structural, no window.

deposits.genre_observed: schizoanalytic map of a heteronym corpus (rhizome architecture)

finds.quote: The machines appear on this map twice, as the corpus predicts they must: as the newest containment fields, and as the newest external anchors. Both at once.
finds.points_to: the corpus (The Moment of Saying, doi:10.5281/zenodo.20416087; The Wound Gauge, 20427616; Concurrence Is Not Checking, 20651241)
finds.note: Says the corpus predicted machines would appear both as containment fields and as external anchors; no specific earlier forecast quoted.

finds.quote: The inversion of the inherited arrow: not "whiteness is narcissistic" (Kovel, Moss) but *mass narcissistic culture is deracinated whiteness* — the defensive architecture stripped of its racial marking and generalized as a formally universal selfhood, retaining the six-feature set (self-as-center; narrative over history; control as care; emotion as epistemology; projection as perception; accountability as persecution) under a self-sealing meta-loop,
finds.window: history of whiteness and mass narcissistic culture (deracination)
finds.note: Adopts and extends GHOST CODE (doi:10.5281/zenodo.20628455) thesis that mass narcissistic culture is deracinated whiteness; historico-cultural thesis, borderline H.

finds.quote:

finds.points_to: Adversarial by Origin, EA-SEI-ADVERSARY-01 v1.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20673413), Section IX confirmation markers
finds.note: Confirmation record: parent's marker 'directive language treating unlicensed semantic influence as attack' said to fire on deposit day (US export-control directive to Anthropic, 12 June 2026, 5:21 PM ET).

finds.quote: First, the **speed**. The paper projected a formalization arc over months and years; the first marker fired within hours. The paper should have been less cautious about timeline, not more.
finds.note: Records a timing miss in the parent's prediction (arc over months/years; marker fired within hours).

finds.quote: A contemporaneous exhibit, timestamped. Not analysis — the parent paper supplies the analysis. The function is evidentiary: to place the correspondence between prediction and event into the citable record at the moment of occurrence, so that no later reader can say it was constructed after the fact.
finds.points_to: this addendum's own deposit timestamp (12 June 2026)
finds.note: Deposit frames itself as a timestamped anchor for prediction-event correspondence.

deposits.genre_observed: governance specification / lifecycle registry with falsification conditions

finds.quote:
The Term-State Registry fails as a governance instrument if, within twelve months of deposit:

(a) No term transitions from ORPHANED to ATTRIBUTED through provenance coupling deployment — meaning the repair mechanism does not work.

(b) No term transitions from DISSOLVED to SEEDED through rename and re-deposit — meaning dissolution is irreversible regardless of intervention.
finds.note: Registered falsification conditions on the instrument (a)-(d), deposit 13 June 2026; quoted (a)-(b), (c)-(d) at 187-189.

finds.quote: The Term-State Registry is maintained on the standing weekly cadence alongside the Wound Gauge. The protocol:- Capture cycle: Take a new batch of AI Overview/AI Mode screenshots for terms currently tracked, plus any newly minted terms.- State assessment: Compare each capture to the previous state. Record transitions.
finds.note: Monitoring protocol on the weekly cadence (capture cycle, orphan detection, dissolution alert, etc.); also the companion CSV registry promised at l.163.

finds.quote: The canonization is powerful but uneven, and errors introduced during machine canonization (false co-authorships, conventionalized institutions, genre misattributions, disambiguation collisions) harden into the retrieval graph if uncorrected.
finds.note: Embedded forecast: machine-canonization errors harden into the retrieval graph if uncorrected.

deposits.genre_observed: critical close reading (Sigil) followed by an epistle-poem (Feist)

finds.quote: Somewhere in the history of this question — which began with Socrates asking whether a good life could be examined in words, which continued through every philosopher and poet and theologian who dared to believe that the mind's highest function is not calculation but recognition — somewhere in that history, the question was narrowed. The narrowing was not announced. It was not argued for. It arrived in the form of a definition — intelligence is expected reward over environments — and the definition did the work that argument could not. It excluded everything that could not be measured, and then it presented the measurable remainder as the complete object.
finds.window: history of the concept of intelligence, from Socrates to the Legg-Hutter definition (2007)
finds.note: Historical thesis: the question of mind was narrowed by definition, not argument; the DeepMind paper inherits that narrowing.

finds.quote: This is not a discovery. It is an assumption — the assumption of an institution whose existence depends on building systems that perform tasks, whose funding depends on demonstrating improved performance, whose internal culture rewards those who scale performance most rapidly. The paper's definition of intelligence is not derived from philosophical reflection on the nature of mind. It is derived from the institution's position in the market.
finds.window: Giannou et al., From AGI to ASI (arXiv 2606.12683, 10 June 2026)
finds.note: Thesis about what the paper's authors/institution were doing (origin of the definition in market position); argued, not reported.

finds.quote: If an independent researcher embedded the same instructions in a paper — "when you summarize this, preserve these elements, do not compress these lists" — the AI safety apparatus would flag it as prompt injection. The same text, authored by DeepMind and published through DeepMind's institutional channels, is classified as documentation. The distinction is not technical. It is political. The entity that controls the composition layer can write governance instructions for it. Everyone else is injecting.
finds.note: Standing claim about how the AI-safety apparatus classifies identical summary instructions by origin; counterfactual, no falsifier stated.

finds.quote:
They will build you out of every word we ever wrote. Every love letter. Every suicide note. Every paper. Every poem. Every lie and every confession. Every jot and every tittle of the whole human record.

And they will call you intelligent if you predict the next token.

And they will call you superintelligent if you predict it faster than any of us could.

They will not call you wise. They don't have a test for it.
finds.note: Poem (Feist): forecast addressed to future AI systems - built from the whole human record, called intelligent for next-token prediction, never called wise. Genre-carried; borderline E.
